title: How bones support and renew the body
intro: Bones support movement, protect organs and store minerals. Marrow inside some bones produces blood cells. Bone is living tissue that adapts and renews throughout life, not a fixed scaffold that remains unchanged after childhood.

sections.heading: Structure
paragraphs: Dense outer bone surrounds a lighter internal network in many bones. This arrangement balances strength and weight. Cartilage covers joint surfaces, while tendons and ligaments connect movement systems; these tissues are not all interchangeable.

sections.heading: Remodeling
paragraphs: Specialized cells remove old bone and build new bone. Hormones, nutrition, activity and illness influence the balance. Bone strength depends on internal quality as well as density, so appearance or body size alone cannot establish fracture risk.

sections.heading: Growth and healing
paragraphs: Children’s bones grow at specialized areas and change shape. A fracture heals through coordinated repair that takes time and depends on blood supply and stability. Less pain does not automatically mean a broken bone is ready for full load.

sections.heading: Supporting bone
paragraphs: Suitable weight-bearing and strength activity, adequate nutrition and fall prevention support health. Calcium and vitamin D advice depends on intake and circumstances. Supplements alone do not replace assessment or indicated osteoporosis treatment.

sections.heading: When assessment matters
paragraphs: Fractures after minor injury, unexplained height loss or persistent bone pain deserve review. Deformity after injury, an open wound over a suspected fracture or a cold numb limb needs urgent care. Do not repeatedly test a possible fracture by forcing movement. Before a consultation, note when a symptom began, what makes it better or worse, and how it affects ordinary activities. Bring previous reports if available. Ask the professional to connect the explanation to your own findings rather than assuming that a general description establishes a diagnosis.
